__description: ArchFlow maps the MyWorkLog source code: every file is a tile, every load a line. Colour stands for the kind of file.
about.diese_karte_zeigt_den_quellcode: This map shows the app's source code: every file is a tile, every line a load relationship. When a page pulls in a script or a stylesheet, that line is drawn here.
about.die_farbe_bedeutet_genau_eine: Colour means exactly one thing — the kind of file:
about.eine_verbindungslinie_traegt_die_f: A connecting line takes the colour of whatever it pulls in. The frames group what belongs together in the app — dashboard, history, report book and so on.
about.ziehen_verschiebt_scrollen_zoomt_i: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. In the overview the names stay hidden because they would be a few pixels tall there; zooming in brings them back. Clicking a tile shows what it loads and who loads it.
about.der_quellcode_von_myworklog_ist: The source code of MyWorkLog is open. Whatever sits here as a tile, you can read there as a file — the map is the overview, the repository is the truth.
about.quellcode_auf_github_ansehen: View the source code on GitHub
about.die_karte_ist_nicht_von: The map is not maintained by hand. An analysis tool reads the repository, follows the references between files and writes the result into a file that this page loads. So it shows the state of the last run, not a hand-drawn wish.
